assessments.reasoning: All five parts of the pinned SPDX json/details/CC-BY-3.0-NL.json share digest 1f8e665b200a05057d8f0bf52e8f5f6c8c7d453aa9c4f390212fad38bdd06225. Part 1 gives Dutch licenseText and isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 3 gives the ID, “Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Netherlands” and both citations.

The GitHub API object for spdx/license-list-data identifies annotated tag 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b as v3.29.0. Its target type is commit and its target is 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, the revision in the detail URL. GitHub reports the tag unsigned.
The publisher capture independently identifies the cited endpoint, its Dutch heading and “CC BY 3.0 NL”. It supplies context for the citation. SPDX owns the membership assertion.

challenge.method: Compared the literal URL against legalcode.nl and the deed. Compared the generated title and clause numbering against the publisher body.
challenge.results: The SPDX citation selects the unsuffixed legal-code URL. SPDX prefixes the Dutch text heading with “Creative Commons” and labels the last item of section 8 “f.” where the publisher’s five-item alphabetical list renders “e.”. The SPDX match value “true” therefore cannot establish literal identity.

limitations: The record documents list membership and citation at one release. Its English name includes Netherlands, which the publisher heading omits. Text identity, legal equivalence, publisher currency, project applicability and reuse remain outside the finding.
reasoning: The generated SPDX 3.29.0 detail record lists CC-BY-3.0-NL. Both crossRef[0].url and seeAlso[0] give https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/nl/legalcode, exactly the publisher acquisition URL.
